master.title: Greece's Public Power Corp to switch on new lignite unit by March
master.content:
325 mots
06-09-2022
17:25
Reuters News
Copyright 2022 Thomson Reuters. All Rights Reserved.

(Recast on opening new lignite-fired plant by March)

ATHENS, Sept 6 (Reuters) - Greece's biggest power utility Public Power Corp (PPC) said on Tuesday that a new coal-fired plant under construction will be switched on by March 2023.

PPC, which is 34% owned by the state, had started building a new unit in the northern Greek region of Ptolemaida before the energy crisis took hold.

The 660 megawatt plant will start trial operation in the second half of the year before its commercial operation begins in the first quarter of 2023, PPC said in a presentation following the announcement of its first-half results.

PPC has pushed back its plan to shut all but one of its coal-fired plants by 2023 as part of a government decision to help safeguard security of Greece's power supplies after Russia curbed gas flows to Europe.

The utility said on Tuesday that it will gradually ramp up coal-fired generation in the coming 12 months, adding that phasing out lignite was still "a strategic decision" for the group.

PPC has been investing heavily in ramping up its green energy capacity to 5.1 gigawatt from 280 megawatt now by 2026.

The utility on Tuesday posted an 8.9% drop in first half core profit on the back of soaring spending for gas purchases and power imports to help cover increased electricity demand.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) came in at 429 million euros ($425.14 million) in the six months to June, down from 471 million euros in the same period last year.

The group reiterated its 2022 guidance for recurring EBITDA at the level seen in 2021. The figure came in at 870 million euros last year.

($1 = 1.0091 euros) (Reporting by Angeliki Koutantou; Editing by Edmund Blair and Marguerita Choy)
